headline: Record assets, surging profit, but clients still exit
summary_short: T. Rowe Price's Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS rose 28.6% y/y to $2.88 as net revenues grew 10.7% to $1,907.4M on record $1.9 trillion AUM, even as clients withdrew a net $6.5 billion during the quarter.
summary_long: Net revenues grew 10.7% y/y (+2.7% q/q) to $1,907.4M as investment advisory fees rose across all asset classes, though the effective fee rate slipped to 38.1bps on a mix shift toward lower-fee products. GAAP operating income rose 13.0% y/y but fell 20.6% q/q, mostly from a $147.5M swing in mark-to-market deferred-compensation costs versus Q1; adjusted operating income (which strips that swing) was roughly flat q/q. Net income rose 25.1% y/y to $632.0M on $369.1M of non-operating gains from seed capital and deferred-comp hedges. Diluted EPS was $2.88 GAAP / $2.57 adjusted. Cash fell 13.3% q/q to $3,234.3M on dividends and buybacks; AUM hit a record $1.9T despite $6.5B of net outflows. Company guided FY2026 effective tax rate to 23.0%-26.0%.

drivers.explanation: Investment advisory fees grew across all asset classes (equity +9.6%, multi-asset +16.1% y/y); the effective fee rate fell to 38.1bps as flows and transfers shifted AUM mix toward lower-fee products, partly offset by market appreciation.

Q/q decline driven by a swing in mark-to-market deferred-compensation liabilities ($126.5M expense vs. a $21.0M credit in Q1) and a higher interim bonus accrual, per the release's own compensation-cost breakdown.
Non-operating income rose to $369.1M from a $48.3M loss in Q1, driven by seed-capital gains and deferred-comp-hedge investment gains, more than offsetting the sequential operating-income decline.

CEO cites record $1.9T AUM and positive May/June flows reflecting client demand in growth areas, continued ETF/SMA expansion and strategic partnerships, while noting fundamental active equity 'remains under pressure.'
